stories.title: Why tech companies are buying up tons of rare old books to train their AI models
stories.summary: NPR's Juana Summers speaks with 404 Media cofounder and reporter Emanuel Maiberg about his investigation into a shipment of rare books which ended up at an Amazon AI training warehouse.

stories.title: More than 1,000 Afghan refugees have been stuck at a camp in Qatar since 2021
stories.summary: More than 1,000 Afghan refugees who fled their homes in 2021 have been stuck in Camp As-Sayliyah, Qatar. They're isolated and unable to leave, despite many having aided U.S. forces during the war.

stories.title: A new competition at a state fair has people yelling like lumberjacks
stories.summary: There's a new contest at the Tennessee State Fare this year: Timber calling.

stories.title: A Paris cafe-bar is a longtime gathering spot for older men of different faiths
stories.summary: A cafe in one of Paris' most historically diverse neighborhoods has long been a gathering spot for Muslims and Jews of Tunisian origin, who've been getting together for decades to play cards and chat.

stories.title: This unusual immune cell in super-agers' bodies could help their longevity
stories.summary: Around age 100, the human body's immune system may make a turn that helps address the common ailments of aging, according to researchers in Japan who study supercentenarians who live to be 110+.

stories.title: On his 19th birthday, a vigil is planned for Mississippi teen Nolan Wells
stories.summary: There's a vigil Wednesday night in Mississippi to mark the birthday of Nolan Wells. The teen who was found dead after being left on a island would have been 19 years old.
